title: Can I SURVIVE Atomic Chess?
summary: Chess.com Atomic chess vs online humans (~1650-1860). Any capture explodes the capturing piece and every non-pawn piece in the surrounding 3x3; blowing up the enemy king wins. Tony loses game 1 (~5:15), wins game 2 by opponent forfeit (~8:10), wins game 3 vs Delhy (~12:22), and loses the last game to a tactic involving his king in the corner (~19:57).
rules: Any capture causes an explosion: the capturing piece, the captured piece and all non-pawn pieces on the 8 surrounding squares are removed; pawns are unaffected by the blast (except a pawn directly captured/capturing).
A king may not capture (it would explode itself); kings can stand adjacent to each other (inferred standard atomic).
Win by exploding the enemy king (or normal checkmate); you may not make a capture that explodes your own king.
win_condition: Blow up or checkmate the opponent's king; goal: win one game (won 2 of 4).

board.theme_notes: standard chess.com green; explosion highlight on capture

current_impl_issues: Impl 'base:Atomic' description says 'destroy every non-pawn piece around them' — matches; verify king-adjacency rules and that the capturing piece also explodes. Opponents are humans (bot strength ~1700).
